comment: Why: the Holy road's cathedral is lit by candle and lantern, so a party that carries its own light is the common case and the dice would meet it more often than a dim floor; the roll bonus of minus one takes back most of that (a church is lit softer than the tower of light, which has minus two). The monsters are what a cathedral keeps once its congregation has fallen: penitents and a choir that lost its god (the cultist tag), stone saints and gargoyles on the buttresses (living armour and the construct tag), the dead of the crypt (the undead tag, for a party that lets its candles go out), the spirits of the votive flames (vexes) and the bell that wakes what sleeps in the belfry. Nothing here is a demon or a brute of the wild: the horror of this place is that everything in it was once devout.
description: The Holy road's cathedral: nave, belfry, cloister and crypt. Candle spirits, a choir that lost its god, stone saints on the buttresses and the dead below.

entries.comment: The breather of the cathedral: one or two of the room's own people (the cultist tag unless the room has a native faction), kneeling until the party comes near. No upper threat, so the minor band never runs dry.
The spirits of the votive candles: a couple of vexes drawn to a bright party. On this road the party is nearly always lit, so this is the common nuisance.
The bats of the belfry, woken by a noisy party as a bell would wake them. A handful, cheap, from the ceiling.

The evergreen standard encounter: the statues of the saints stepping down from their niches, the mod's living armour. The id is explicit so the first floors, where the construct tag is thin, still have a reliable fight.

The caster pair of the cathedral: a choir of the cultist tag that lost its god, with the church's stone guardians for bodyguards. Casters first, so the entry always has them; the guards are trimmed first when the budget is short.
The walls are alive: gargoyles on the buttresses turn their heads and drop. Placed close (range 10-22) over three places with a short hunt, because the point is that they were always there.
The rare dark entry of this road: a party that lets its candles go out wakes the dead of the crypt, who rise from under the floor. One to three, never scaled by the party.
Priests who hear what they should not: an evoker with a few conjured candle-spirits, for a party that has been in the nave long enough to be noticed.

The loud brute: the stone saint of the belfry (an iron golem, a hundred health, five points of budget) wakes to a noisy party as the bell would wake a chapter. One body, a lot of health; hard band only and from threat 3, where a hard budget can pay for it.
The mimic-style surprise of a church: the knight's tomb opens. Armoured dead step out of the side chapels with a priest behind them. Close range and a short hunt.

A cult that calls on what the church was built to keep out: cultists first and the demon they called with them (the two tags are allies, so they never fight each other). The two kinds are the whole fight: a caster crowd and a brute.
The wave of the cathedral: the great bell tolls and every candle-spirit in the nave comes at once, many in three places with a priest behind them.
The late ambush: the dead and the armoured walk out of the crypt and the side chapels together, from two sides. Only for parties of two or more.
